key_insight: The paper proposes a real-time, loss-minimizing power-sharing controller for hybrid energy storage by analytically checking KKT conditions instead of solving heavy optimization problems online.
engineering_relevance: This enables efficient dispatch of complementary storage technologies in renewable plants, improving ancillary-service capability while remaining practical for deployment.
method: Model each storage device with detailed power-dependent efficiency curves rather than constant-efficiency assumptions.
Formulate power sharing to minimize total losses and verify optimality through Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions analytically.
Implement and validate the controller in MATLAB/Simulink and OPAL-RT for real-time operation.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on a 10 MW PV plant with a 2.5 MW/5 MWh lithium-ion battery and a 2.5 MW/5 MWh redox-flow battery, with both numerical simulation and real-time OPAL-RT demonstration.
watch_item: Performance depends on the accuracy of the efficiency curves and the hardware/controller assumptions, so model mismatch could reduce optimality in practice.
paper_title: Optimal Power Sharing for Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Based on Karush-Kuhn-Tucker Conditions
